- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply mean reversion to prior 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast using 7-day moving average or apply decay factor to sentiment weight.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias if price > 10% above 14-day average.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If model forecast is <10% below true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply upward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
